title: Oklahoma M2.5+ earthquake clustering in 2010-2026 faded within about 13 months, unlike tectonic aftershocks; tapered ETAS fit to 2020 forecast the 2021-2026 count and pure Omori ETAS 5 times too many
abstract: Question: how long does earthquake-to-earthquake clustering last in Oklahoma induced seismicity, how much of the 2021-2026 rate is the late tail of the 2011-2020 sequences, and which clustering model forecasts the decline? Approach: we fitted space-time ETAS models to 10,806 OGS M2.5+ events (2010-2026) with a free background rate in each 0.2-degree cell and 6-month bin, and an Omori-Utsu kernel with or without an exponential taper exp(-t/tau). We applied the same code to three Japanese tectonic sequences (JMA) and to synthetic catalogs, and we made forecasts from fits that end in 2018 and 2020. Results: the data strongly prefer a taper: tau = 405 days (335-474 over six background designs), with a log-likelihood gain of 680 for one parameter (194 at M3+). The tectonic controls gave gains of 0.0-9.0 and tau of 3.6 years to infinity, and synthetic pure-Omori catalogs gave gains of 2.7-10.3. Parents of M3.5+ had longer, near-Omori tails (tau 6.5 years, p 1.09); small parents had short, swarm-like clustering. Productivity per parent fell from 0.556 (2014-2016) to 0.398 (2020-2026), and the ratio of all events to independent events fell from 5.1-5.8 to 3.4; productivity did not increase with current local injection. Of the 413 events in 2021-2026, the tapered models give 25-41% to independent events (about 22 per year, 3 times the 1980-2008 rate of all events) and 14-44% to descendants of pre-2021 events; pure Omori gives 40-58%. From a 2020 fit, pure Omori ETAS forecast 2,018 events from earlier events alone (4.9 times the observed 413); tapered models with a decaying background forecast 378 and 412, but too few in 2024-2026. From a 2018 fit, all models forecast too many (tapered 1,763 for 788). The 2021-2026 independent count follows the 2014-2016 count of each cell, not current injection (slopes 0.14-0.35, upper bounds below 0.6). Limitations: the free background cannot hold slow tails inside one cell-bin; ETAS clustering in Oklahoma includes swarms driven by common pressure changes; OGS magnitude practice and network density changed after 2016; the profile interval is model-conditional; many variants were compared.

display.caption: Taper tests. a: Oklahoma M2.5+ log-likelihood gain over the pure Omori kernel against a fixed taper time; the diamond is the free fit (405 days). b: gain of a free taper for Oklahoma (blue) and three Japanese tectonic sequences (aqua), same code and settings. c: synthetic catalogs with a pure Omori truth (gray) or a 400-day taper (orange): recovered taper time and gain.

Out-of-sample yearly M2.5+ counts from ETAS fits that end in 2020 (a-c) and 2018 (d-e): offspring of earlier events only (orange), plus a decaying background (aqua) or a constant background (blue); means and 90% ranges of 300 simulations (100 for pure Omori); black dots are observed counts.

Yearly OGS M2.5+ counts (black), ETAS independent (background) events (blue) and events that descend from pre-2021 events (orange) for the tapered (a) and pure Omori (b) models; 2026 is scaled to 12 months. The dashed line is the 1980-2008 rate of all events.
